newsitem.title: USA: Panel says U.S. inflation overstated by 1.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Panel says U.S. inflation overstated by 1.1 pct.

text.p: A congressionally-appointed commission on Wednesday estimated that government statistics overstate inflation by 1.1 percentage points a year, a finding that could have major implications for the federal budget and the whole economy.

The panel, led by Stanford University economist Michael Boskin, recommended a series of actions by the Clinton administration and Congress to fix the problem, including potential legislation to alter the way tax brackets and costly programmes like Social Security are adjusted for cost-of-living changes.

"Congress and the President must decide whether they wish to continue widespread substantial over-indexing of various federal spending programmes and features of the tax code," the five-member panel said in their report.
If benefits and taxes are to be adjusted appropriately, Congress and the President should pass a law to change the way that is done, the report added.
The commission's report, quoting Congressional Budget Office estimates, said the upward bias in the Consumer Price Index would add $148 billion to the federal budget deficit by 2006 if not fixed.

The report highlighted several reasons for the upward bias to the CPI, including difficulty in capturing the effects of changes in consumers' spending patterns and the impact of the introduction of new products.
